q: Put the Zephyr build pipeline in order, from the inputs to the image.
items: Merge the board devicetree with your overlays
Resolve Kconfig: defaults + board defconfig + prj.conf into .config
CMake selects which source files to compile
Compile and link zephyr.elf, then convert to .hex/.bin
explain: Devicetree comes first, because Kconfig depends on it: many driver symbols default to `y` only if a matching enabled node exists (`DT_HAS_<compat>_ENABLED`). Kconfig then produces `.config` / `autoconf.h`, and CMake uses those `CONFIG_*` symbols to choose sources (`zephyr_library_sources_ifdef`). Only then does any C get compiled. Hardware description and feature selection are both settled before your code is.

q: You add `CONFIG_BME280=y` to `prj.conf` and call `DEVICE_DT_GET(DT_NODELABEL(bme280))`. The link fails with `undefined reference to '__device_dts_ord_42'`. In `build/zephyr/.config` you find `# CONFIG_BME280 is not set`. What is the most likely cause?
code:
config BME280
    bool "BME280 sensor"
    depends on DT_HAS_BOSCH_BME280_ENABLED
    depends on SENSOR
options: prj.conf is ignored when an overlay exists
A `depends on` isn't satisfied (e.g. `CONFIG_SENSOR` is off, or there's no enabled bosch,bme280 node), so Kconfig dropped your `=y` with only a warning and kept building
You need `select BME280` in prj.conf instead of `=y`
The driver is compiled but the linker removed it as unused, so add `-Wl,--no-gc-sections`
explain: A `=y` in prj.conf is a *request*. If a `depends on` is false, Kconfig drops the assignment, prints a warning ("was assigned the value 'y' but got the value 'n'. Check these unsatisfied dependencies: ...") and the build carries on. A typo such as `CONFIG_BME28O=y` would have stopped the build instead. With no driver built, nothing defines the device instance for your node, hence the missing `__device_dts_ord_*` symbol. Fix the dependency: enable `CONFIG_SENSOR`, and make sure the devicetree has an enabled node with `compatible = "bosch,bme280"`. `select` only exists inside Kconfig files, not prj.conf. prj.conf and overlays work together, and the linker isn't the culprit: the driver was never compiled at all. (Had it compiled and linked, a `device_is_ready()` of false would point at a failed init instead: the chip not answering on the bus.)

options: `west.yml` (the manifest) pins every repository in the workspace (Zephyr, HALs, MCUboot...) to a revision
`west update` checks out all manifest projects at their pinned revisions
`west build` replaces CMake: Zephyr doesn't use CMake
`west flash` programs the board using a runner such as J-Link, pyOCD or OpenOCD
explain: west is the meta-tool: a multi-repo workspace manager driven by the manifest (`west init` / `west update`), plus a command runner. `west build` is a *wrapper around* CMake (and Ninja), not a replacement. Because the manifest pins every dependency, committing `west.yml` makes the whole firmware's dependency tree reproducible.

q: What's the difference between `depends on` and `select` in Kconfig?
options: They are synonyms; `select` is just the newer spelling
`depends on X` means this symbol can only be enabled if X is; `select X` forces X on whenever this symbol is on (even overriding X's own dependencies)
`depends on` is evaluated at runtime, `select` at build time
`select` makes a symbol user-visible in menuconfig, `depends on` hides it
explain: `depends on` is a precondition: when it's false, the symbol is forced to `n`. `select` is a push: turning this symbol on turns the selected one on too. `select` ignores the selected symbol's own dependencies, which can create broken configurations, so it's mostly used for small library-like symbols (e.g. a sensor driver selecting `I2C`). Both are evaluated at build time. Kconfig has no runtime component.

q: Your team ships the same app on two boards and wants a debug variant with logging and asserts. Which layout is idiomatic Zephyr?
options: Edit `build/zephyr/.config` by hand for each variant
Copy the board's `.dts` into the app and edit it per variant
`prj.conf` for the common config, `boards/<board>.overlay` + `boards/<board>.conf` per board, and a `debug.conf` fragment added with `-DEXTRA_CONF_FILE=debug.conf`
Use `#ifdef DEBUG` everywhere and pass `-DDEBUG` to gcc
explain: Layering is the Zephyr way: common Kconfig in `prj.conf`, per-board hardware and config next to it in `boards/`, and build-variant fragments on the command line. CI can then build the matrix. `.config` is regenerated on every build, so hand edits vanish. Forking the board `.dts` stops you from getting upstream fixes. Ad-hoc `-D` flags bypass Kconfig, so subsystems (logging, asserts) never get configured.
